practices.practice: Keep the cluster connection string out of source control (eg. in an environment variable) and use a secret store (for example Azure Key Vault) or managed identity retrieval for production secrets.
practices.prior_belief: Store the cluster connection string in an environment variable (e.g., DOCUMENTDB_URI) and never commit it; for production use a secret store such as Azure Key Vault and grant your app managed identity access to fetch it at runtime.
practices.source_name: Migrate from Amazon DocumentDB to Azure DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility)
practices.how_found: migrate amazon documentdb replace connection string store in config 'Azure DocumentDB migrate from Amazon'

practices.practice: Create and reuse a single MongoClient/driver client per process (module/global singleton) rather than creating a new client per request.
practices.prior_belief: Reuse a single MongoClient instance per process (create at startup, share across threads/tasks) and close it on shutdown; avoid making a new client per request. Tune pool sizes with maxPoolSize/minPoolSize in the connection options.

practices.practice: Always connect with TLS (tls=true) and do not disable certificate validation in production.
Implement retries for transient faults using exponential backoff and handle rate-limiting (HTTP/Mongo 429) with jitter and honoring any server Retry-After hints.
practices.prior_belief: Implement retries with exponential backoff for transient errors and rate limiting: catch 429 (Request Rate Too Large) and network/timeout errors, use the server-provided Retry-After header when present, and retry with jitter.

practices.practice: Use cluster tier / vCore and storage sizing (M-tiers) to provision capacity for indexing and vector workloads; Azure DocumentDB uses cluster tiers (e.g., M30+) and not cosmos RU/s as the primary provisioning knob for the managed MongoDB-compatible service.
practices.prior_belief: Provision throughput (RU/s) appropriate for indexing and vector search: estimate ingestion, embedding compute and query load and use autoscale or set sufficient RU/s for the sample database/collection to avoid frequent 429s; increase RU during index creation and bulk loads.
practices.source_name: Integrated vector store in Azure DocumentDB
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB vector index DiskANN HNSW IVF 'vector-diskann' 'M30'

practices.practice: Create conventional single-field and compound indexes for fields used in filters, grouping and sorts (e.g., channel, created_at/timestamp) and prefer designing compound indexes by ESR (Equality → Sort → Range) for common predicates.
practices.prior_belief: Create conventional indexes on fields used for filtering/aggregation (e.g., channel, topic tags, created_at) and consider a compound index for common compound predicates (e.g., {channel:1, created_at:1}) to accelerate the aggregation pipelines.

practices.practice: Use TTL indexes (expireAfterSeconds) on a date field to implement time-based retention so old raw feedback can be purged automatically.
practices.prior_belief: For time-based retention, use a TTL policy/index (expireAfterSeconds) to automatically purge raw feedback after the retention period rather than manual delete jobs.

practices.practice: Store embeddings as number[] with a fixed dimensionality, include metadata for the embedder (model name and dimension) alongside vectors, and (when using cosine similarity) normalize vectors at write time so queries can rely on consistent vector semantics.
practices.prior_belief: Store deterministic embeddings with a fixed vector dimension and a field name (e.g., embedding: [float,...]) and validate length on write; if using cosine similarity, also store normalized vectors (unit length) to simplify search/score calculations.

practices.practice: Pick the vector index type to match scale: use vector-ivf for small sets (<10k), vector-hnsw up to tens of thousands, and vector-diskann for production-scale (M30+); tune index build/query parameters (m/efConstruction for HNSW; maxDegree/lBuild and query-time lSearch for DiskANN) to balance recall, memory and latency.
practices.prior_belief: When creating vector indexes tune ANN index parameters for HNSW/IVF: set a sensible M (e.g., 16–64) and efConstruction (e.g., 100–200) at index creation to balance recall and memory; set efSearch at query time (higher for better recall).

practices.practice: If a native server command for search/indexing isn't available in your environment, implement a graceful fallback path (for example store embeddings and use client-side nearest-neighbour search) rather than failing hard.
practices.prior_belief: If the managed cluster returns CommandNotSupported for vector/text index creation, fall back to storing embeddings and performing nearest-neighbor matching client-side (or with manual approximate search logic) and keep index-creation attempts guarded with graceful fallback.
practices.how_found: createSearchIndexes CommandNotSupported fallback; 'Azure DocumentDB createSearchIndexes unsupported' 'createSearchIndexes not supported fallback client side embeddings'

practices.practice: Prefer atomic update/patch operations ($set, $push, $inc, patch) to replace entire documents when enriching records to avoid large rewrites and the higher RU cost of full-replaces.
practices.prior_belief: Design documents to avoid frequent large rewrites: use atomic update operators ($set, $push, $inc) to modify only changed fields (e.g., add sentinel fields sentiment, topics, embedding) instead of replacing entire documents on enrichment.
practices.source_name: Understand request units consumption in Azure Cosmos DB
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB updates cost more RUs 'update vs create cost' 'request units document operations'

practices.practice: Use bulk operations (insertMany, bulkWrite) for batch ingestion and tune batch size to the service limits to reduce round-trips and improve throughput; Azure DocumentDB supports large batch writes and documents per-batch limits (documentdb docs note batch limits).
practices.prior_belief: Use bulk operations (insert_many, bulk_write) when ingesting batches of feedback to reduce round-trips and improve throughput, and throttle bulk size to avoid exhausting RU/s during large loads.
practices.source_name: Document size and batch write limits in Azure DocumentDB
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB batch write limits insertMany 'max writes per batch 25000'

practices.practice: Enforce lightweight JSON Schema validation at the collection level using $jsonSchema to require essential fields (text, channel, timestamp/created_at, embedding dimensions) so downstream queries and pipelines can assume basic invariants.
practices.prior_belief: Enforce a lightweight schema/validation (JSON Schema validator) at the collection level to require essential fields (text, channel, created_at, embedding length, sentiment) so downstream aggregation and embedding logic can assume schema invariants.

practices.practice: Store embedding metadata (model name and dimension) with each vector and rebuild indexes when you change embedding dimension/model to avoid silent correctness errors.
practices.prior_belief: Keep the embedding dimension and vector data type consistent across documents (e.g., 1536 floats) and store metadata about the embedder (model name + version) alongside each embedding to allow model upgrades without corrupting search semantics.

practices.practice: Enable diagnostic settings and slow-query logs and alert on CPU/memory/IOPS/connection saturation; use explain() / query plan analysis to detect COLLSCANs and adjust indexes accordingly.
practices.prior_belief: Monitor slow queries and index usage; use explain() on expensive aggregation pipelines and create/adjust indexes based on the query plan. Regularly inspect cluster metrics (RU consumption, index storage, latency).

practices.practice: For production clusters enable in-region HA (availability zones) and consider cross-region replica for DR; be explicit about replication/consistency tradeoffs when designing topology.
Use Private Endpoint / firewall rules to restrict access to your cluster; prefer Private Link for production and integrate with private DNS for proper SRV resolution.

practices.practice: Prefer the DocumentDB-native search path: create search indexes with createSearchIndexes and query with the $search aggregation stage rather than relying on community text indexes and $text.

When upgrading encryption key ownership use Customer-Managed Keys (CMK) and user-assigned managed identities; CMK must be prepared in Key Vault in the same region with required permissions and consideration for key rotation/availability.

practices.practice: Use deterministic document IDs or composite keys (for example source_channel + source_id) and upsert semantics to make ingestion idempotent and simplify deduplication.
practices.prior_belief: Use deterministic document IDs or a composite unique key (e.g., source_channel + source_id) to make ingests idempotent and simplify deduplication of the same feedback item across channels.

practices.practice: Store timestamps in UTC as date/ISODate values and index the timestamp field to make time-window aggregations ($bucket, $dateTrunc) efficient.
practices.prior_belief: For aggregation pipelines that compute time-series sentiment (by channel/topic/time window), ensure created_at is indexed and store timestamps in UTC and as an ISODate so $bucket or $dateTrunc operations are efficient.

practices.practice: Regularly back up important data and use the platform-provided automatic backups (DocumentDB provides continuous backups with a documented retention window) and test restores rather than relying only on ad-hoc JSON exports.
practices.prior_belief: Regularly back up important data and know the provider’s backup/restore options; for critical datasets enable continuous or frequent backups and test restore procedures rather than relying solely on exported JSON snapshots.

practices.practice: Avoid storing raw PII in cleartext in the database; either omit, pseudonymize, mask, or encrypt sensitive customer identifiers and consider PII detection/redaction before indexing/searching.
practices.prior_belief: Avoid storing raw PII in cleartext; for identifiers or sensitive customer fields either omit them from the enrichment store, pseudonymize or encrypt them with client-side field-level encryption before storing.
practices.source_name: Security Frame: Sensitive Data | Mitigations / Data encryption in Azure DocumentDB

practices.practice: When enriching text with LLMs store source_text, the structured extracted fields, and metadata (model name/version) so data can be validated and reprocessed if extraction prompts or models change.
practices.prior_belief: When embedding or enriching via LLMs, perform the extraction (sentiment, topics, quote) deterministically where possible, validate the output, and store source_text and the canonical extracted fields to allow reprocessing if parsing prompts/models change.
